text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein urges a "white revolution against weakness and backwardness," says "no force in the world can stand against attaining just and comprehensive (Middle East) peace".
- A sit-in protest in front of Israeli trade fair planned by broad-based campaign against convening the exibition on Wednesday; organisers call again for boycott of the exhibition.
- Prime Minister Kabariti to meet Omani Sultan Qaboos, hands a letter from King Hussein to the Omani ruler on bilateral ties and Middle East peace developments.
- King Hussein calls on Arab governments to be active partners with the private sector, not competitors.
- Jordan's Islamic Action Front (IAF) delegation visits Damascus, hold talks with Syrian officials on "dangers facing Arab nation".
- 25 percent of publicly listed companies in the Amman Financial Market (AFM) are highly attractive, says a newly released report.
- Head of contractors union calls for setting up mergers among firms to consolidate the sector.
- Supply ministry increases inspection of foodstuffs ahead of preparations for the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan.
- King meets Arab League chief; both review peace process, Arab affairs and league's role.
